findings: src/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp: the replication gate depends only on aggregate properties: every aggregate must be NOT_ORDER_DEPENDENT, none may be DISTINCT, and the replicated state array must fit in 1MiB. It names no tables, columns, literals or data sizes, and it applies to any low-cardinality perfect-hash GROUP BY.

Correctness: AddChunk only changes which replica a row's address points to. Combine sends every source replica to target replica 0. Scan folds the table's own replicas 1..K-1 into replica 0 once before it reads any results. The source phase is single-threaded (GetData has no MaxThreads override), so the replicas_folded flag has no race. Destroy now covers all total_groups*replica_count tuples. That matches the old behaviour of destroying every slot, and combined-from states being destroyed afterwards is how Combine between tables already works with ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE.

Each CombineStates batch can contain the same target address several times (replicas 1..3 all go into one group's replica 0). The standard AggregateExecutor::Combine loops over entries one at a time, so this is safe for the gated aggregates (sum, count, min/max, bool, avg, quantile and mad).

extension/core_functions/aggregate/algebraic/avg.cpp: NOT_ORDER_DEPENDENT is set only on the exact-state avg variants (int16, int32, int64, int128 and interval, plus decimal through BindDecimalAvg). The double avg is still order-dependent, so floating-point results do not change. The flag also lets the ordered-aggregate optimizer drop ORDER BY inside these avgs, which is semantically correct.

Cost: state initialisation and combine work grow 4x, but they scale with the number of groups, not rows, and the size cap bounds them. No work is moved outside the timing, and thread and memory settings are unchanged.
